citation: S. J. Haake (1989), PhD thesis, Aston University, tables 3.3, 3.4 and 3.10.

conditions.lie: driver teed 35 mm, other clubs on fairway 5 mm

targets.note: Angles below horizontal in, above it out. Backspin positive. Table 3.3 does not name the green, so these rows carry no green class.
Angles below horizontal in, above it out. Backspin positive. Table 3.3 does not name the green, so these rows carry no green class.

Mean of the 3 impacts of one machine setting at Ganton, table 3.4. Ganton is of Haake's slipping type, the greens that keep backspin when the ball lands with more than about 350 rad/s, which he found free-draining with under 60% Poa annua. The earlier implementation has no green class. Backspin positive.
